verdicts.factCheck: Every public source of the finding was fetched again on 2026-11-23 and says what the finding quotes. Cargo.toml at tag v0.0.7.3-rc.1 of okx/xlayer-reth lists crates/intercept and crates/rcs-filter as workspace members and takes every reth crate from okx/reth revision f60420aaac6457295a38b66bd544bab28ab6ec5d. rpc.xlayer.tech answered web3_clientVersion three times with reth/v2.3.0-f60420a/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xlayer/v0.0.7, so the public endpoint runs that line. crates/rcs-filter/src/config.rs at the tag: FilterConfig::default() sets enabled to false and rcs_base_url to an empty string, validate() refuses enabled with an empty URL, and max_native_transfers_per_tx and max_event_bindings_per_tx default to 10,000. rcs_capture.rs lines 381 to 400: observe_native_transfer returns early for a zero value or a self transfer, otherwise raises observed_count and sets the overflow flag above the limit. The comment states that the count never rolls back. The call, create and selfdestruct hooks feed it. context.rs lines 110 to 127: LimitExceeded maps to Screen::Deny. Lines 734 to 735: the capture inspector is built only inside if let Some(filter). Lines 1001 to 1047: Deny and Drop mark the transaction invalid and remove it from the pool, and AuditPending marks it invalid for this iteration and leaves it in the pool. Lines 505 to 640 (execute_sequencer_transactions, the path for deposits) contain no reference to the filter, and line 847 keeps deposits out of the pool loop, so deposits are outside the filter as the finding says. The bridge interceptor in crates/intercept matches BridgeEvent logs of one configured bridge contract and is off by default. It does not look at PoolManager activity. The main branch config.rs adds max_callstack_observations_per_tx with default 10,000. The releases page shows v0.0.7 of 27 August with the entry feat(rcs): add the Risk Control Service transaction filter and RPC audit layer and the sentence that the release is for X Layer Testnet only, v0.0.7.3 of 30 October with the coordinated upgrade due by November 10, 2026, and v0.0.7.3-rc.1 of 5 November as a mandatory patch. The notes of the last two do not mention the filter. On chain: eth_getProof on xlayer.drpc.org for 0x59055c0ef0be92018b33f877a3eB816355791727 at latest (about block 76,675,525) still returns storage root 0x84d6f8a2145c426cd92452349876bd7386c8dbff1ee9b5d0476ab923d098a89d, the root the finding reports for block 76,668,710, so the blacklist storage has not changed since. eth_getStorageAt returns implementation 0xe44bfef30cfd8ecbfb917d78fa2ac215b3397f8e and admin 0x57ffb399eb2d8fb1831001ba893483bc13bd8c2f. I did not walk the trie again. Block 76,589,451 has gasUsed 97,312,645 against a limit of 210,000,000, and transaction 0x349b40443331dbfec3a5ecd1fb666b0dc59935b76f4b688546c4d4278864f04f used 95,673,102 gas with no log. I did not repeat the eth_feeHistory scan of 1,142,553 blocks or the eleven traces. The OKX report says that screening logic is written into the protocol and that for Exchange OS the protocol layer keeps a sanctioned and risk address library. It does not name the sequencer filter. The link that stays unconfirmed is the one the finding itself names: whether the mainnet sequencer starts with the filter enabled, and which rules the service delivers. No public interface exposes the flag and I found no operator statement. I looked for a primary source that contradicts the finding and found none.
verdicts.codeCheck: take is the only function an ordinary caller has that moves a currency out of the PoolManager: src/PoolManager.sol:291-297 debits the caller and calls currency.transfer, which is a native CALL with value or an ERC-20 transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:40-88). take carries onlyWhenUnlocked (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99), and the flag is set only inside unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27), which calls back into the caller and reverts unless every delta is zero (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Removing liquidity (src/PoolManager.sol:145-184), burning a claim (src/PoolManager.sol:332-336) and swapping (src/PoolManager.sol:187-227) carry the same modifier. An exit is therefore always one transaction that enters unlock, and it leaves the chain only if the sequencer includes it or if it arrives as an L1 deposit. The second outflow, collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57), needs msg.sender to equal protocolFeeController, which is the zero address on X Layer (eth_call protocolFeeController() on 0x360e68faccca8ca495c1b759fd9eee466db9fb32 returns 0). Nothing in src/ reads block time, block number or the coinbase, so a delayed exit loses no funds by itself. A take of the native currency is one internal value transfer and a take of a token is none, so an ordinary exit is far below the rule independent limit of 10,000 transfers. A transaction through a hookless pool runs no third party code apart from the token contracts, so an ordinary account cannot push a stranger's exit over that limit. The hazard needs the operator.
verdicts.corrections: The actor operator and the severity low stand. The verdict stays plausible because the enabled state of the filter on the mainnet sequencer is unconfirmed. Correction 1: the gas needed to exceed the native transfer limit is overstated. In revm 40.0.3 (tag v112, call_helpers.rs lines 92 to 105) the caller of a CALL with value pays 9,000 plus 100 for a warm account and the forwarded gas, and the 2,300 stipend is added to the callee's gas without charge, so a transfer to a warm account that runs no code costs 6,800 gas net. 10,001 such transfers cost about 68,000,000 gas plus loop overhead, against the 91,000,000 the finding states. The conclusion is unchanged, because the finding inspected every transaction above 40,000,000 gas and found at most four internal transfers. The open lead should quote about 69,000,000 gas for a test transaction. Correction 2: mechanism step 1 says funds leave only through take. collectProtocolFees is a second outflow (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57). It is limited to accrued protocol fees and to the fee controller, which is the zero address on X Layer, so the statement holds for ordinary users. Correction 3: the v0.0.7.3 release notes name okx/reth revision 81573d2 as the sync point. The revision f60420a that the endpoint reports is the one pinned by the patch tag v0.0.7.3-rc.1.

sources.supports: Workspace members crates/intercept and crates/rcs-filter, reth crates pinned to okx/reth revision f60420aaac6457295a38b66bd544bab28ab6ec5d, revm 40.0.3.
enabled is false by default, a base URL is required when enabled, both per transaction limits default to 10,000.
observe_native_transfer counts every nonzero transfer between two different accounts, never rolls the count back and sets a sticky overflow above the limit.

A capture outcome other than complete maps to Screen::Deny, the inspector exists only with a filter handle, a deny verdict removes the transaction from the pool, and the deposit path does not consult the filter.
The bridge interceptor is off by default and matches BridgeEvent logs of one configured bridge contract only.
The main branch adds max_callstack_observations_per_tx with default 10,000.

v0.0.7 introduced the filter and is marked for testnet only, v0.0.7.3 required a coordinated mainnet upgrade by 10 November 2026, v0.0.7.3-rc.1 of 5 November is a mandatory patch, and the notes of the last two do not mention the filter.
The caller is charged the forwarded gas first and the call stipend is added afterwards, so an unused stipend returns to the caller and a plain value transfer costs 6,800 gas net.
OKX states that screening logic is written into the protocol and that a sanctioned and risk address library is kept at the protocol layer for Exchange OS. The sequencer filter is not named.

clearedSpotChecks.check: A1 on Celo at the production tag: can a value in the PoolManager's transient slots (unlock flag, deltas, synced currency and reserves) cross from the fee debit into the main call, or from one transaction into the next, for a transaction that pays gas in a fee currency.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read handler.rs at tag celo/reth-v1.0.10. cip64_rollbackable_debit_and_deduct_caller opens a journal checkpoint, runs the debit, and on success calls checkpoint_commit and then transient_storage.clear() before the main call (lines 616 to 672). On rejection it reverts the checkpoint. core_contracts.rs call_inner clears transient storage after every committing system call (lines 211 to 250), and credit_gas_fees uses that path (erc20.rs lines 103 to 137). The journal file of celo-org/revm at revision bd28f9420c250df2a5c4a6d8103b51ae06b5c222 is byte identical to bluealloy/revm tag v107 (I compared the two downloads with cmp), and commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize each clear the transient map (lines 154, 188, 246). On the code side the unlock flag cannot outlive a successful main call, because unlock sets it back before returning (src/PoolManager.sol:113) and a revert undoes it. The one value that can stay set is a synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), and the credit runs token code that never calls settle. The debit and the credit name the transaction caller as the debited account, both at the tag and on the main branch, and the PoolManager cannot be a transaction caller.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Can an ordinary account make the Celo node call the PoolManager, or a contract of its own, with msg.sender equal to address(0), by naming that address as the fee currency of a transaction. The protocol fee controller is address(0), and collectProtocolFees checks the sender only (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57).
clearedSpotChecks.note: handler.rs at the tag, lines 509 to 588: currency_exchange_rate(fee_currency) on the fee currency context runs first and returns an invalid transaction error for an unregistered address. The balance read and debit_gas_fees come after it. The system calls target the fee currency and FeeCurrencyDirectory only. On chain at block 83,543,949: the registry resolves FeeCurrencyDirectory to 0x15F344b9E6c3Cb6F0376A36A64928b13F62C6276, its owner is the Governance contract 0xD533Ca259b330c7A88f74E000a3FaEa2d63B7972, and getCurrencies() returns 20 addresses, none of which is the PoolManager. eth_call of collectProtocolFees on the Celo PoolManager from an ordinary address reverts with 0x48f5c3ed (InvalidCaller). From the zero address with amount 0 it returns 0, and with amount 1 it reverts with an arithmetic panic, because protocolFeesAccrued is 0 for the native currency, the CELO token, USDC, USDT and USDm. This matches src/ProtocolFees.sol:48-55: the caller check passes for the zero address and the checked subtraction caps the payout at accrued fees. Even a caller that could act as the zero address would be limited to setting a protocol fee of at most 0.1 percent and collecting what accrues after that (src/ProtocolFees.sol:35-41). One addition: USDm accepts debitGasFees(PoolManager, 1) in an eth_call from the zero address and rejects it from an ordinary address, and the other 19 registered currencies also reject the call from an ordinary address (block 83,544,082). The PoolManager's balance of a fee currency is therefore protected by the node passing only the transaction caller, which the source confirms.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Critic gap of cycles 2 and 5: repeat the special address sweep with a forwarding stub at the PoolManager address, so that tx.origin differs from msg.sender as in a real take, sync or hook call. Sixteen shapes (empty calldata with and without value, transfer with 0 and 1, balanceOf, ten hook selectors, unlockCallback) against the predeploy range, the precompiles, the Celo core contracts, the X Layer system contracts, the EntryPoints and the usual preinstalls, with the stub's native balance read before and after every call.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I repeated a sample of the shapes with the PoolManager address as sender, without a stub, and did not rerun the full sweep of about 630 address and chain pairs. Celo, block 83,543,949: CELO.balanceOf(PoolManager) equals eth_getBalance(PoolManager) (0x14b4f48ca0407db0662 wei), CELO.transfer(0xdead, 1) from the PoolManager returns true, an empty call with 10^15 wei to the CELO token reverts, and both an empty call with value and transfer(0xdead, 1) to 0xfd fail with a precompile error. Of the 20 registered fee currencies at block 83,544,082, 16 answer transfer(0xdead, 0) with true and four (0x0E2A3e05, 0x2F25deB3, 0x0357Ee22, 0x857BF24e) answer balanceOf and revert on transfer, which matches the four adapters of the sweep. X Layer, block 76,675,701: Wrapped OKB and 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 accept an empty call with value, 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000016 reverts with value, 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000013 returns the L1 block number 0x194078d for both an empty call and balanceOf, and 0xfd answers both shapes with empty data, as an account without code does. The conclusion follows from the code for every one of these classes. The balance that sync and settle compare lives in one transient slot pair (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), a settle with value reverts while a token is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356), and settle and settleFor are the only payable functions, so one inflow cannot be credited under both address(0) and the CELO token. An address that returns 32 bytes other than 1 to transfer fails the check at src/types/Currency.sol:64-74, and an address whose balanceOf is constant inside one transaction yields a payment of zero (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). A hook response must start with the called selector (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152).
